question.problem: If $(x+5)$ is a factor of $p(x)=3{x}^{2}+14x+c,$ then $c=$
question.worked_solution:
According to the factor theorem, if $(x-r)$ is a factor of $p(x),$ then the root $x=r$ is also a root of $p(x).$ 

Here, we are considering the factor $(x+5).$ The root of this factor can be found by setting the factor equal to $0$ and solving:

$$
\begin{aligned}x+5 & =0 \\ x & =-5\end{aligned}
$$

According to the factor theorem, then, since $(x+5)$ is a factor of $p(x),$ the root $x=-5$ is also a root of $p(x).$ This means $p(-5)=0,$ so we have

$$
\begin{aligned}p(-5) & =0 \\ 3(-5)^{2}+14(-5)+c & =0 \\ 75-70+c & =0 \\ c & =-5.\end{aligned}
$$
